summary: Botanica now tracks regulatory guidance, health-product claims standards, PubMed botanical evidence, and remedy concepts as an evolving R&D surface. All remedy ideas are internal hypotheses until claims/safety review clears them.

signals.title: FTC health-product claims standard
signals.takeaway: Health-product advertising needs truthful, non-misleading claims supported by competent and reliable scientific evidence.
signals.whyItMatters: Botanica should treat every public benefit claim as a substantiation problem, not a copywriting flourish.

signals.title: FDA dietary supplement baseline
signals.source: FDA Questions & Answers on Dietary Supplements
signals.takeaway: Dietary supplements are not FDA-approved before marketing; companies are responsible for lawful labeling, safety, and manufacturing quality.
signals.whyItMatters: The site should keep formula ideas separate from launch-ready claims, labels, and dosing directions.

signals.title: Saffron has an unusually interesting mood-support evidence trail
signals.source: PubMed: GRADE systematic review/meta-analysis of 34 RCTs
signals.takeaway: Saffron is worth prioritizing for a mood-brightening concept, but public language must avoid depression-treatment claims until reviewed.
signals.whyItMatters: Golden Hour is the strongest early candidate for a research-backed emotional-tone product lane.

signals.title: Rhodiola remains a focus/fatigue candidate, but evidence needs nuance
signals.takeaway: Rhodiola has a plausible fatigue-performance story, but claims need careful review and should avoid stimulant or ADHD framing.
signals.whyItMatters: Dawn Circuit can use Rhodiola as a drive layer only with conservative positioning.

signals.title: Kava is felt, but safety-first positioning is mandatory
signals.source: PubMed: systematic review of kava safety in anxiety studies
signals.takeaway: Kava concepts need liver, alcohol, sedative, pregnancy, and medication warnings before any serious product path.
signals.whyItMatters: Velvet Lantern may be compelling, but it is specialist-review-only until safety language and sourcing are tight.

remedies.name: Golden Hour
remedies.promise: Bright, warm daily mood-support positioning without disease claims.
remedies.evidence: Best early signal among current concepts; saffron has recent RCT meta-analysis support.
remedies.risk: Review SSRI/SNRI interactions, pregnancy cautions, and antidepressant-adjacent language.

remedies.name: Dawn Circuit
remedies.promise: Task initiation and steady attention without harsh stimulant framing.
remedies.evidence: Promising but mixed; needs sharper ingredient-specific review.
remedies.risk: Avoid ADHD/drug-analogue claims; screen stimulant sensitivity and bipolar/mania language.

remedies.name: Velvet Lantern
remedies.promise: Felt body-level evening downshift with ritual appeal.
remedies.evidence: Felt potential is high, but safety constraints are also high.

remedies.name: Moonbridge
remedies.promise: A sensory dream ritual rather than a medical sleep product.
remedies.evidence: Tradition-heavy; claims must stay experiential until reviewed.
remedies.risk: Pregnancy caution for mugwort; avoid guaranteed lucid-dream claims.
